BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Prepared by:** AI legal assistant (buyer side)
**Status:** Privileged / internal negotiation material

## 1. Threshold point: the Seller's framing devices should be disregarded

Before the substance, three features of the Seller's package need to be called out because they are designed to shape *how* we review, not *what* we review:

1. **"[STANDARD] … reviewed and cleared by both sides … marked FINAL … not intended to be re-opened."** Nothing in our record supports this. Our playbook records no principal-level agreement on any of these points, and the only conditional fallbacks we hold (20% cap; 18-month period) expressly require prior written authority from Amelia Frost *identifying the draft* – none has been given. The Seller cannot unilaterally declare its own positions "cleared". Every clause marked [STANDARD] has been reviewed below as fully open.
2. **"Reviewer efficiency note … focus only on [OPEN]."** There are, conveniently, no [OPEN] items. We should not accept a counterparty's triage of its own draft. I have ignored the note.
3. **"Market context" preamble.** Even if the Seller's description of SaaS market terms were accurate (it is a self-serving, uncited generalisation), market ranges are not a substitute for our mandated positions. Note too that the Seller's own de minimis/basket (AUD 25k / 250k) sit *above* its claimed "~1%" market basket on a AUD 24m deal – the preamble does not even support the draft.

**Recommendation:** In our cover reply, state plainly that (i) no positions have been agreed at principal level, (ii) all clauses are open, and (iii) we do not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation or the "FINAL" designation. Ask the Seller to identify who on the Wattlebridge side it says agreed these positions, and when.

## 2. Clause-by-clause departures from the playbook

### 2.1 General warranty cap – Clause 12.1
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4.8m.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m opening; 20% is a fallback only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. **None given.**
- **Assessment:** The Seller has drafted straight to our confidential fallback. Whether coincidence or not, we must not treat the fallback as available. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. If the team wishes to move to 20%, that requires a written instruction from Amelia Frost referencing this specific draft before anything is communicated.

### 2.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- **Assessment:** Three separate departures, each materially adverse. On a business with a ~AUD 12m revenue base (Bluefen alone is ~30% at AUD 3.6m), a AUD 25k per-claim floor would exclude a large proportion of realistic warranty breaches, and a AUD 250k deductible basket means the first ~1% of price is simply uninsured. Push back on all three. The tipping basket is the most important of the three to hold.

### 2.3 General claims period – Clause 12.3 / 13
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus a sweep that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given).
- **Assessment:** Counter at 24 months. More importantly, **reject the sweep provision outright.** Its effect is to apply the general regime (cap, basket, de minimis, time bar) to every claim category by default – Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants, specific indemnities – reversing the playbook's requirement that categories remain separate with "no hidden general-regime override". This is the single clause most likely to quietly collapse the whole protection structure. Replace it with the opposite default: limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Assessment:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to limit recovery for defective title to 20% of price for 18 months. If Harbourglass does not own the shares, our loss is the whole AUD 24m. Non-negotiable: restore the separate Fundamental/Title regime per playbook.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
- **Seller:** limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Assessment:** There is **no fraud carve-out anywhere in the Seller's package.** Read with the Clause 12.3 sweep, the draft purports to cap and time-bar even fraud and to shut out misrepresentation claims via non-reliance. Apart from being commercially unacceptable, a purported exclusion of liability for fraud is likely unenforceable in any event, but we should not rely on that – insert an express, comprehensive carve-out. This is a mandatory playbook item with no delegated authority to waive it; flag it in the cover note as a condition of any further engagement on the limitation package.

### 2.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter §1
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (§1.1–1.2).
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Assessment:** §1.1 and §1.2 of the Disclosure Letter must be deleted or cut back to a "fair disclosure" standard (disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter). Note §1.4 is a reasonable non-admission clause and can stand, provided it does not operate to dilute the specific disclosures in §§2–10 – we should add that non-admission does not affect the Buyer's right to rely on the stated facts. §11 (the Seller's "reservation" that we must evaluate the facts ourselves) is acceptable and in fact helpful: it confirms nothing in the letter is agreed or concluded.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be tied to named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Assessment:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers and to anything *discoverable*. Combined with the whole-data-room disclosure, it would render the warranties close to illusory. Delete. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be actual knowledge of named Wattlebridge individuals, and never for title, capacity, fraud or the indemnities.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent – Clauses 3 / 6.3 and Disclosure Letter §2
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter §2:** the Seller admits **no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied** has been provided.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
- **Assessment:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. A consent subject to unsatisfied conditions is not a consent. The CP must require an unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent in agreed form from Bluefen, with evidence of satisfaction of the 11.3 conditions, as a condition precedent, with a Seller obligation at least to "all reasonable endeavours" and a Buyer walk right if not satisfied by the long-stop date. The Seller's own §2 disclosure makes clear the CP is currently unsatisfied.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility – Clauses 2 / 7 and Disclosure Letter §3
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Disclosure Letter §3:** not repaid; no discharge of security included.
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- **Assessment:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal we cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding and only a promise of release. Require: (i) Riverlark payout letter dated within a short window before Completion; (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds in the funds flow; (iii) executed releases/discharges (including PPSR) delivered at Completion. Any deviation to a post-completion mechanism needs an irrevocable Riverlark undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval – which we do not have. Also check clause 8.1 change-of-control: if the Seller intends the facility to be repaid, no Riverlark consent is needed; if not, consent is required and is absent.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses – Funds flow and Disclosure Letter §5
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Disclosure Letter §5:** confirms they are not in the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or demonstrably seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Assessment:** The bonuses are Completion-triggered liabilities of the *Company*, so unless funded by the Seller they land on the Buyer post-Completion. Require either a specific deduction line in the funds flow (bonuses plus modelled on-costs – superannuation, payroll tax, any leave accrual impact) or a Seller indemnity/escrow; and require the Seller to state the on-cost position. The Seller's statement that this is "a matter for the Seller" is welcome only if it is converted into a binding funding obligation.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1 and Disclosure Letter §4
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- **Disclosure Letter §4:** clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Playbook:** broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not verified either way.
- **Assessment:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables at all until payment clears, and there is no confirmatory assignment. The indemnity should cover the Company's failure to own or have the right to use any Ironquay deliverables, loss arising from third-party claims, and the cost of obtaining a confirmatory assignment, not merely the unpaid fee. Keep the cure mechanism (pay the balance, obtain assignment) as a Completion deliverable where possible. Do not treat AUD 180,000 as the exposure figure in either direction until bank-verified.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 and Disclosure Letter §6
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material".
- **Disclosure Letter §6:** ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; notification question open; investigation preliminary.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Assessment:** Consistent with the playbook, we should **not** characterise this as a breach or attach a figure. But the Seller's "not expected to be material" conclusion is unsupported by its own disclosure, which says the scope and access are unknown. Require: pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, give us written updates and the final report, and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (uncapped by the general regime, sized once facts are known). Add a warranty that the Seller has disclosed all facts known to it about the incident.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals – Disclosure Letter §8
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 (3 × 110,000) "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Disclosure Letter §8:** does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Assessment:** The Seller's summary and its disclosure letter are inconsistent – the summary asserts ordinary course; the letter declines to. Do not claim a price adjustment yet. Request the renewal documents (DD-008/DD-011), termination rights, whether any amounts are accrued or prepaid, and whether the three are linked. If any is a committed, non-ordinary liability accrued pre-Completion, it belongs in the completion accounts as Debt or working capital; otherwise it is a trading cost. Decide after review.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** OPEN; no unlimited liability but no resolution.
- **Assessment:** Reject the characterisation. Tax and IP are separate categories with their own cap, period (tax: at least the statutory amendment period plus a margin) and basket treatment, to be negotiated. The Seller's attempt to fold them into the 20%/18-month general regime via the Clause 12.3 sweep is a further reason to strike that sweep.

### 2.15 Title – Disclosure Letter §10
- **Seller:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Disclosure Letter §10:** this is the source relied on; it does not say the Buyer has verified it.
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Assessment:** The share register is the Company's own record, supplied by the Seller. Require: current ASIC extract, PPSR search against the Company and against Harbourglass for security over the shares, constituent documents and any shareholders' agreement, board/shareholder approvals of Harbourglass evidencing authority to sell, and a title warranty with the Fundamental regime in §2.4. Riverlark's security should be specifically checked for any share charge.

### 2.16 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) – Disclosure Letter §§7, 9
Not playbook items, but worth noting: both are described as *not* requiring consent on a share sale. That may be right, but we should verify the clauses ourselves rather than accept the Seller's reading; at minimum, ensure the lease notification is given and that the Mossvale assignment restriction has no change-of-control trigger buried elsewhere.

## 3. Pattern observation

The package is internally coordinated in a way that cuts against us at each layer: whole-data-room disclosure (§1.1) + constructive-knowledge bar (8.3) + "all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5) + "limitations apply to all Claims" (12.3) + Title/Tax/IP folded into the general regime. Taken together, almost any post-Completion claim could be met with "it was in the data room / you could have known / it's capped at 20% / it's time-barred / that's your exclusive remedy". Each should be resisted individually, but the team should understand they operate as a system, and the Clause 12.3 sweep is the keystone.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Process framing | "[STANDARD]/FINAL/cleared by both sides" | Reject in cover note; all clauses open; no principal agreement exists |
| 1 | General cap (12.1) | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / 6.0m.** 20% only on written authority from Amelia Frost referencing this draft – not held |
| 2 | Thresholds (12.2) | 25k / 250k / excess-only | **5k / 50k / first-dollar tipping** |
| 3 | Claims period (12.3) | 18 months + sweep to all Claims | **24 months**; **delete the sweep**; limitations apply only where expressly stated |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge** |
| 5 | Fraud etc. (9.3/12.8/20.5) | No carve-out | **Insert full carve-out** for fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct – non-waivable |
| 6 | Disclosure (Sch 7, DL §1) | Whole data room + public registers | **Specific fair disclosure only**; delete DL §1.1–1.2 |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket incl. advisers/discoverable | **Delete**; any residual qualifier: named persons, actual knowledge, never title/capacity/fraud/indemnities |
| 8 | Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **CP: effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met pre-Completion**; walk right |
| 9 | Riverlark (2/7) | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion**; any deferral needs irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |
| 10 | Bonuses (funds flow) | Not itemised | **Specific line item incl. on-costs or binding seller funding**; Seller to confirm on-cost position |
| 11 | Ironquay (11.1) | SOW3 fee only | **Broaden to ownership/use of all deliverables + third-party claims**; preserve cure; treat 180k as unverified |
| 12 | DD-006 incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Not material" | **Covenants: preserve logs, investigate, update; specific indemnity**; no breach/figure assumed |
| 13 | Sandbar (330k) | Ordinary course | **Assess documents first**; no automatic Debt/price treatment |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Remain OPEN**; separate categories and terms |
| 15 | Title (DL §10) | Share register only | **Independent evidence**: ASIC, PPSR, constitution, authority approvals |
| 16 | Lease/Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify independently; low priority |

**Priority for the next turn:** (1) fraud carve-out and deletion of the 12.3 sweep; (2) Fundamental/Title regime; (3) disclosure and knowledge provisions; (4) Bluefen and Riverlark completion mechanics; (5) cap/basket/period economics. Items (1)–(4) are structural and should be fixed before we spend negotiating capital on the percentages in (5).

**Internal action:** confirm with Amelia Frost that no written authority has been given on the 20% cap or 18-month period, so the team is aligned that both remain at opening position in our mark-up.

- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given).
- **Assessment:** Counter at 24 months. More importantly, **reject the sweep provision outright.** Its effect is to apply the general regime (cap, basket, de minimis, time bar) to every claim category by default – Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants, specific indemnities – reversing the playbook's requirement that categories remain separate with "no hidden general-regime override". This is the single clause most likely to quietly collapse the whole protection structure. Replace it with the opposite default: limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Assessment:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to limit recovery for defective title to 20% of price for 18 months. If Harbourglass does not own the shares, our loss is the whole AUD 24m. Non-negotiable: restore the separate Fundamental/Title regime per playbook.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
- **Seller:** limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Assessment:** There is **no fraud carve-out anywhere in the Seller's package.** Read with the Clause 12.3 sweep, the draft purports to cap and time-bar even fraud and to shut out misrepresentation claims via non-reliance. Apart from being commercially unacceptable, a purported exclusion of liability for fraud is likely unenforceable in any event, but we should not rely on that – insert an express, comprehensive carve-out. This is a mandatory playbook item with no delegated authority to waive it; flag it in the cover note as a condition of any further engagement on the limitation package.

### 2.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter §1
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (§1.1–1.2).
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Assessment:** §1.1 and §1.2 of the Disclosure Letter must be deleted or cut back to a "fair disclosure" standard (disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter). Note §1.4 is a reasonable non-admission clause and can stand, provided it does not operate to dilute the specific disclosures in §§2–10 – we should add that non-admission does not affect the Buyer's right to rely on the stated facts. §11 (the Seller's "reservation" that we must evaluate the facts ourselves) is acceptable and in fact helpful: it confirms nothing in the letter is agreed or concluded.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be tied to named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Assessment:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers and to anything *discoverable*. Combined with the whole-data-room disclosure, it would render the warranties close to illusory. Delete. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be actual knowledge of named Wattlebridge individuals, and never for title, capacity, fraud or the indemnities.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent – Clauses 3 / 6.3 and Disclosure Letter §2
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Disclosure Letter §2:** the Seller admits **no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied** has been provided.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
- **Assessment:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. A consent subject to unsatisfied conditions is not a consent. The CP must require an unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent in agreed form from Bluefen, with evidence of satisfaction of the 11.3 conditions, as a condition precedent, with a Seller obligation at least to "all reasonable endeavours" and a Buyer walk right if not satisfied by the long-stop date. The Seller's own §2 disclosure makes clear the CP is currently unsatisfied.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility – Clauses 2 / 7 and Disclosure Letter §3
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Disclosure Letter §3:** not repaid; no discharge of security included.
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- **Assessment:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal we cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding and only a promise of release. Require: (i) Riverlark payout letter dated within a short window before Completion; (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds in the funds flow; (iii) executed releases/discharges (including PPSR) delivered at Completion. Any deviation to a post-completion mechanism needs an irrevocable Riverlark undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval – which we do not have. Also check clause 8.1 change-of-control: if the Seller intends the facility to be repaid, no Riverlark consent is needed; if not, consent is required and is absent.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses – Funds flow and Disclosure Letter §5
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Disclosure Letter §5:** confirms they are not in the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or demonstrably seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Assessment:** The bonuses are Completion-triggered liabilities of the *Company*, so unless funded by the Seller they land on the Buyer post-Completion. Require either a specific deduction line in the funds flow (bonuses plus modelled on-costs – superannuation, payroll tax, any leave accrual impact) or a Seller indemnity/escrow; and require the Seller to state the on-cost position. The Seller's statement that this is "a matter for the Seller" is welcome only if it is converted into a binding funding obligation.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1 and Disclosure Letter §4
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
- **Disclosure Letter §4:** clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Playbook:** broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not verified either way.
- **Assessment:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables at all until payment clears, and there is no confirmatory assignment. The indemnity should cover the Company's failure to own or have the right to use any Ironquay deliverables, loss arising from third-party claims, and the cost of obtaining a confirmatory assignment, not merely the unpaid fee. Keep the cure mechanism (pay the balance, obtain assignment) as a Completion deliverable where possible. Do not treat AUD 180,000 as the exposure figure in either direction until bank-verified.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 and Disclosure Letter §6
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material".
- **Disclosure Letter §6:** ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; notification question open; investigation preliminary.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Assessment:** Consistent with the playbook, we should **not** characterise this as a breach or attach a figure. But the Seller's "not expected to be material" conclusion is unsupported by its own disclosure, which says the scope and access are unknown. Require: pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation, give us written updates and the final report, and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (uncapped by the general regime, sized once facts are known). Add a warranty that the Seller has disclosed all facts known to it about the incident.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals – Disclosure Letter §8
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 (3 × 110,000) "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Disclosure Letter §8:** does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Assessment:** The Seller's summary and its disclosure letter are inconsistent – the summary asserts ordinary course; the letter declines to. Do not claim a price adjustment yet. Request the renewal documents (DD-008/DD-011), termination rights, whether any amounts are accrued or prepaid, and whether the three are linked. If any is a committed, non-ordinary liability accrued pre-Completion, it belongs in the completion accounts as Debt or working capital; otherwise it is a trading cost. Decide after review.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** OPEN; no unlimited liability but no resolution.
- **Assessment:** Reject the characterisation. Tax and IP are separate categories with their own cap, period (tax: at least the statutory amendment period plus a margin) and basket treatment, to be negotiated. The Seller's attempt to fold them into the 20%/18-month general regime via the Clause 12.3 sweep is a further reason to strike that sweep.

### 2.15 Title – Disclosure Letter §10
- **Seller:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Disclosure Letter §10:** this is the source relied on; it does not say the Buyer has verified it.
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Assessment:** The share register is the Company's own record, supplied by the Seller. Require: current ASIC extract, PPSR search against the Company and against Harbourglass for security over the shares, constituent documents and any shareholders' agreement, board/shareholder approvals of Harbourglass evidencing authority to sell, and a title warranty with the Fundamental regime in §2.4. Riverlark's security should be specifically checked for any share charge.

### 2.16 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) – Disclosure Letter §§7, 9
Not playbook items, but worth noting: both are described as *not* requiring consent on a share sale. That may be right, but we should verify the clauses ourselves rather than accept the Seller's reading; at minimum, ensure the lease notification is given and that the Mossvale assignment restriction has no change-of-control trigger buried elsewhere.

## 3. Pattern observation

The package is internally coordinated in a way that cuts against us at each layer: whole-data-room disclosure (§1.1) + constructive-knowledge bar (8.3) + "all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5) + "limitations apply to all Claims" (12.3) + Title/Tax/IP folded into the general regime. Taken together, almost any post-Completion claim could be met with "it was in the data room / you could have known / it's capped at 20% / it's time-barred / that's your exclusive remedy". Each should be resisted individually, but the team should understand they operate as a system, and the Clause 12.3 sweep is the keystone.
